s.d: ὀδυνάω, -ῶ (ὀδύνη), [in LXX: [[zechariah 9 5|Zec.9:5]] (חוּל), [[zechariah 12 10|Zec.12:10]] (מָרַר hi.), [[lamentations 1 13|La 1:13]] (דָּוֶה), Wis.14:24, al. ;] to cause pain or suffering; pass. and mid., to suffer pain, be tormented or greatly distressed: [[luke 2 48|Luk.2:48 16:24-25]] (ὀδυνᾶσαι, see M, Pr., 53 f.); before ἐπί, [[acts 20 38|Act.20:38.]]† (AS)
ὀδύνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for יָגוֹן, מַר, etc. (26 words in all) ;] pain, distress, of body or mind : [[romans 9 2|Rom.9:2]], [[1-timothy 6 10|1Ti.6:10]].† (AS)
ὀδυρμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὀδύρομαι, to lament), [in LXX : [[jeremiah 31 15|Jer.31:15]] (תַּמְרוּר), 2Ma.11:6 * ;] lamentation, mourning: [[matthew 2 18|Mat.2:18]] (LXX), [[2-corinthians 7 7|2Co.7:7.]]† (AS)

1. as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist , οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται (Odyssey by Homer); τεθνηῶτος, μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος (Odyssey by Homer); οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι he is no more , (Euripides); θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (Iliad by Homer); ἐσσόμενοι posterity, (Iliad by Homer); ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων (Demosthenes Orator):—;so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔστι Τροία (compare Troja fuit) , (Euripides) 2. of things, to be, exist , εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ ἡ τράπεζα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last , (Thucydides) 3. to be , opposite to appearing to be , as esse to videri , τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true story, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν (Thucydides); τῶι ὄντι, Lat. revera, in reality, in fact, (Plato Philosophus) 4. followed by the Relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς, no one , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; εἰσὶν οἵ, Lat. sunt qui, (Thucydides), etc.; ἐστὶν ἅ some things , (Thucydides); also ἔστιν οἵ, for εἰσὶν οἵ, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;so withrelat. Particles, ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπη, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somewhere , or somehow , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπως in some manner , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 5. ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, like πάρεστι, it is possible , (Homer), attic 6. to be , Copula connecting predicate with subject, both being in the same case, (Homer), etc. 7. sometimes εἶναι with Part. represents finite Verb, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πεφυκός ἐστι = πέφυκε, (Aristophanes Comicus) 8. the Inf. is redundant in some phrases, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών II); τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι quantum in illis esset , (Thucydides); τὸ σύμπαν εἶναι (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ νῦν εἶναι (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)
Ὀζείας (Rec. Ὀζίας), -ου, ὁ (Heb. עֻזִּיָּה), Uzziah: [[matthew 18 1|Mat.18:1-35 9:1-38]].† (AS)
ὄζω [in LXX: [[exodus 8 14|Exo.8:14]] (בָּאַשׁ)* ;] to smell (i.e. emit a smell): [[john 11 39|Jhn.11:39.]]† (AS)

ὅθεν adv., whence; (a) of direction or source: [[matthew 12 44|Mat.12:44]], [[luke 11 24|Luk.11:24]], [[acts 14 26|Act.14:26 28:13]]; = ἐκεῖθεν ὅπου, [[matthew 25 24|Mat.25:24, 26]] (cf. Thuc., i, 89, 3); ὅ. γινώσκομεν, [[1-john 2 18|1Jn.2:18;]] (b) of cause, whence, wherefore: [[matthew 14 7|Mat.14:7]], [[acts 26 19|Act.26:19]], [[hebrews 2 17|Heb.2:17 3:1 7:25 8:3 9:18 11:19]].† (AS)
ὀθόνη, -ης, ἡ (of Semitic origin, cf. Heb. אֵטוּן, yarn) 1. fine linen (Hom., al.). 2. Later, a sheet or sail: [[acts 10 11|Act.10:11 11:5]].† (AS)

ὀθόνιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὀθόνη, which see), [in LXX: [[judges 14 13|Jdg.14:13]] (סָדִין), [[hosea 2 5|Hos.2:5]], 9 (פִּשְׁתֶּה)* ;] a piece of fine linen, a linen cloth; [[luke 24 12|Luk.24:12]] (WH, R, mg., om.), [[john 19 40|Jhn.19:40 20:5-7]].† (AS)

οἰκεῖος, -α, -ον (οἶκος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, שְׁאֵר, etc.; in [[isaiah 58 7|Isa.58:7]], οἰ. τοῦ σπέρματος for בָּשָׂר ;] in or of the house (opposite to ξένος, ἀλλότριος); (a) of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods; (b) of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: [[1-timothy 5 8|1Ti.5:8;]] with genitive of person(s), of the family of: metaphorically, τ. θεον, [[ephesians 2 19|Eph.2:19;]] τ. πίστεως (Lft., in l), [[galatians 6 10|Gal.6:10.]]† SYN,: συγγενής, ἴδιος (see Cremer, 446; Deiss., BS, 123) (AS)

οἰκέτης, -ου, ὁ (οἰκέω), [in LXX for עֶבֶד ;] a house-servant: [[luke 16 13|Luk.16:13]], [[romans 14 4|Rom.14:4]]; pl., [[acts 10 7|Act.10:7]], [[1-peter 2 18|1Pe.2:18]] (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4:30 6:11, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.)† SYN.. see: διάκονος (AS)

οἰκέω, -ῶ (οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁב ;] (a) trans., to inhabit: with accusative, [[1-timothy 6 16|1Ti.6:16;]] (b) intrans., to dwell: before μετά (of married life), [[1-corinthians 7 12|1Co.7:12-13;]] metaphorically, before ἐν: ἀγαθόν, [[romans 7 18|Rom.7:18;]] ἁμαρτία, [[romans 7 20|Rom.7:20;]] πνεῦμα θεοῦ, [[romans 8 9|Rom.8:9, 11]], [[1-corinthians 3 16|1Co.3:16]] (cf. ἐν-, κατ-, ἐν-κατ-, παρ-, περι-, συν-οικέω).† (AS)

οἴκημα, -τος, τό (οἰκέω), [in LXX: [[ezekiel 16 24|Eze.16:24]] (גַב), Tob.2:4, Wis.13:15 * ;] a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms (e.g. brothel. Hdt., ii, 121; cf. Ez, l.with), a prison (Thus., iv, 47 f.); [[acts 12 7|Act.12:7.]]† (AS)
οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό (οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), [in LXX: 2Ma.11:2, 3Ma.2:15 * ;] a habitation: Ju 6; trop., [[2-corinthians 5 2|2Co.5:2.]]† (AS)

οἰκία, -ας, ἡ (οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;] a house, dwelling: [[matthew 2 11|Mat.2:11 7:24-27]], [[mark 1 29|Mrk.1:29]], al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, [[luke 8 27|Luk.8:27;]] εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. ([[matthew 8 14|Mat.8:14]], al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, [[john 14 2|Jhn.14:2.]] Metaphorical, (a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: [[2-corinthians 5 1|2Co.5:1;]] (b) of property (as בַּיִת, [[genesis 45 18|Gen.45:18]], LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; [[1-kings 13 8|3Ki.13:8]], LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): [[mark 12 40|Mrk.12:40]], [[luke 20 47|Luk.20:47]]; (with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: [[matthew 12 25|Mat.12:25;]] with genitive of person(s), [[john 4 53|Jhn.4:53]], [[1-corinthians 16 15|1Co.16:15]] SYN.: οἶκος, which in Attic law denoted the whole estate, οἰκία, the dwelling only. In cl. poets οἶκος has also the latter sense, but not in prose, except in metaphorically usage, where it signifies both property and household. The foregoing distinction is not, however, consistently maintained in late Greek; cf. MM, ii, xvii, and see Thayer, see word οἰκία (AS)

οἰκία, -ας, ἡ (οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;] a house, dwelling: [[matthew 2 11|Mat.2:11 7:24-27]], [[mark 1 29|Mrk.1:29]], al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, [[luke 8 27|Luk.8:27;]] εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. ([[matthew 8 14|Mat.8:14]], al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, [[john 14 2|Jhn.14:2.]] Metaphorical, (a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: [[2-corinthians 5 1|2Co.5:1;]] (b) of property (as בַּיִת, [[genesis 45 18|Gen.45:18]], LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; [[1-kings 13 8|3Ki.13:8]], LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): [[mark 12 40|Mrk.12:40]], [[luke 20 47|Luk.20:47]]; (with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: [[matthew 12 25|Mat.12:25;]] with genitive of person(s), [[john 4 53|Jhn.4:53]], [[1-corinthians 16 15|1Co.16:15]] SYN.: οἶκος, which in Attic law denoted the whole estate, οἰκία, the dwelling only. In cl. poets οἶκος has also the latter sense, but not in prose, except in metaphorically usage, where it signifies both property and household. The foregoing distinction is not, however, consistently maintained in late Greek; cf. MM, ii, xvii, and see Thayer, see word οἰκία (AS)
οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν (οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος belonging to the household, one's own: [[matthew 10 36|Mat.10:36;]] opposite to οἰκοδεσπότης, [[matthew 10 25|Mat.10:25.]]† (AS)
οἰκο-δεσποτέω, -ῶ (οἰκοδεσπότης) to rule a household: [[1-timothy 5 14|1Ti.5:14.]]† (AS)

οἰκο-δεσπότης, -ου, ὁ (οἶκος, δεσπότης), the master of a house, a householder: [[matthew 10 25|Mat.10:25 13:27 20:11 24:43]], [[mark 14 14|Mrk.14:14]], [[luke 12 39|Luk.12:39 13:25 14:21]]; ἄνθρωπος οἰ., [[matthew 13 52|Mat.13:52 20:1 21:33]]; pleonast., oἰ. τ. οἰκίας, [[luke 22 11|Luk.22:11]] (see Bl., § 81, 4).† (AS)

οἰκοδομέω, -ῶ (οἰκοδόμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּנָה ;] to build a house, to build: absol., [[luke 11 48|Luk.11:48 14:30 17:28]]; οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, the builders (as [[psalms 118 22|Psa.118:22]], בָּנָה), [[matthew 21 42|Mat.21:42]], [[mark 12 10|Mrk.12:10]], [[luke 20 17|Luk.20:17]], [[1-peter 2 7|1Pe.2:7]]" (LXX) ; ἐ π ̓ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰ., proverb., [[romans 15 20|Rom.15:20;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[galatians 2 18|Gal.2:18;]] πύργον), [[matthew 21 33|Mat.21:33]], [[mark 12 1|Mrk.12:1]], [[luke 14 28|Luk.14:28]]; ἀποθήκας, [[luke 12 18|Luk.12:18;]] ναόν, [[mark 14 58|Mrk.14:58;]] pass., [[john 2 20|Jhn.2:20;]] οἰκία, [[luke 6 48|Luk.6:48;]] with accusative of thing(s) before dative of person(s) (cf. [[genesis 8 20|Gen.8:20]], [[ezekiel 16 24|Eze.16:24]]), [[luke 7 5|Luk.7:5]], [[acts 7 47|Act.7:47, 49]]; accusative before ἐπί, [[matthew 7 24|Mat.7:24, 26]] [[luke 6 49|Luk.6:49]]; πόλιν ἐπ ̓ ὄρους, [[luke 4 29|Luk.4:29;]] of rebuilding, or restoring, [[matthew 23 29|Mat.23:29 26:61 27:40]], [[mark 15 29|Mrk.15:29]], [[luke 11 47|Luk.11:47]], Metaphorical, τ. ἐκκλησίαν, [[matthew 16 18|Mat.16:18;]] of the growth of Christian character (cf. בָּנָה, in [[psalms 28 5|Psa.28:5]], [[jeremiah 24 6|Jer.24:6]], al.), to build up (AV, edify): absol., [[acts 20 32|Act.20:32]], [[1-corinthians 8 1|1Co.8:1 10:23]]; with accusative of person(s), [[1-corinthians 14 4|1Co.14:4]], [[1-thessalonians 5 11|1Th.5:11]]; pass., [[acts 9 31|Act.9:31]], [[1-corinthians 14 17|1Co.14:17]], [[1-peter 2 5|1Pe.2:5]]; of blameworthy action (AV, embolden), [[1-corinthians 8 10|1Co.8:10]] (cf. ἀν-, ἐπ-, συν-οικοδομέω).† οἰκο-δόμος, -ου, ὁ (οἶκος + δέμω, to build), [in LXX for בָּנָה, etc. ;] a builder: [[acts 4 11|Act.4:11.]]† (AS)

οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ (οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: [[1-chronicles 29 1|1Ch.29:1]] A (בִּירָה), [[ezekiel 17 17|Eze.17:17 40:2]] (בָּנָה, מִבְנֶה), Sir.22:16 40:19, al. ;] = cl. οἰκοδομία (which see), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.), 1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: [[romans 14 19|Rom.14:19 15:2]], [[1-corinthians 14 26|1Co.14:26]], [[2-corinthians 10 8|2Co.10:8 13:10]], [[ephesians 4 29|Eph.4:29]]; with genitive obj., [[1-corinthians 14 12|1Co.14:12]], [[2-corinthians 12 19|2Co.12:19]], [[ephesians 4 12|Eph.4:12, 16]]; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., [[1-corinthians 14 3|1Co.14:3.]] 2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: [[matthew 24 1|Mat.24:1]], [[mark 13 1|Mrk.13:1-2]]; metaphorically, [[1-corinthians 3 9|1Co.3:9]], [[2-corinthians 5 1|2Co.5:1]], [[ephesians 2 21|Eph.2:21]].† (AS)
οἰκοδομία, -ας, ἡ (οἰκοδομέω), the act of building: metaphorically, [[1-timothy 1 4|1Ti.1:4]] (BE for οἰκοδομία, which see).† (AS)

οἰκονομέω, -ῶ (οἰκονόμος), [in LXX: [[psalms 112 5|Psa.112:5]] (כּוּל pilp.), 2Ma.3:14 * ;] to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., [[luke 16 2|Luk.16:2;]] hence, generally (see: οἰκονομία), to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).† (AS)

οἰκονομία, -ας, ἡ (οἰκονομέω), [in LXX: [[isaiah 22 19|Isa.22:19, 21]] (מַצָּב, מֶמְשָׁלָה)* ;] 1. prop. (Plat., Arist.), the office of οἰκονόμος, stewardship: [[luke 16 2|Luk.16:2-4.]] 2. In later writers (Plut., al.; see AR on [[ephesians 1 10|Eph.1:10;]] MM, xviii), generally, administration, dispensation: [[1-corinthians 9 17|1Co.9:17]], [[ephesians 1 10|Eph.1:10 3:2, 9]], [[colossians 1 25|Col.1:25]], [[1-timothy 1 4|1Ti.1:4]].† (AS)

οἰκονόμος, -ου, ὁ (οἶκος + νέμω, to manage) [in LXX chiefly for עַל ;] 1. prop., the manager of a household or estate, a house- or land-steward (usually a slave or freedman): [[luke 12 42|Luk.12:42 16:1, 3 16:8]], [[1-corinthians 4 2|1Co.4:2]], [[galatians 4 2|Gal.4:2]]; ὀ οἰ. τ. πόλεως (RV, treasurer; cf. I [[esther 4 49|Est.4:49]]), [[romans 16 23|Rom.16:23]]. 2. Metaphorical (in wider sense; cf. οἰκονομία), an administrator, a steward: of Christian ministers, [[1-corinthians 4 1|1Co.4:1]], [[titus 1 7|Tit.1:7]]; of Christians generally, [[1-peter 4 10|1Pe.4:10.]]† (AS)

οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;] 1. prop., a house, dwelling: [[acts 2 2|Act.2:2 19:16]]; with genitive poss., [[matthew 9 6|Mat.9:6]], 7 [[mark 2 11|Mrk.2:11]], [[luke 1 23|Luk.1:23]], al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, [[john 2 16|Jhn.2:16;]] προσευχῆς, [[matthew 21 13|Mat.21:13]], al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, [[matthew 12 4|Mat.12:4]], al.; the temple, [[matthew 21 13|Mat.21:13]], al.; metaphorically of a city: [[matthew 23 38|Mat.23:38]], [[luke 13 35|Luk.13:35]]; of the body, [[matthew 12 44|Mat.12:44]], [[luke 11 24|Luk.11:24]]; of Christians, [[1-peter 2 5|1Pe.2:5;]] ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, [[mark 2 1|Mrk.2:1]], [[1-corinthians 11 34|1Co.11:34 14:35]]; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, [[acts 2 46|Act.2:46 5:42]]; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., [[luke 7 10|Luk.7:10 15:6]]; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, [[acts 8 3|Act.8:3 20:20]]; εἰς (κατ ̓) οἶκον, with genitive (Bl., §46, 9), [[mark 8 3|Mrk.8:3]], [[luke 14 1|Luk.14:1]], [[romans 16 5|Rom.16:5]], al. 2. By meton., a house, household, family: [[luke 10 5|Luk.10:5]], [[acts 7 10|Act.7:10]], [[1-corinthians 1 16|1Co.1:16]], [[1-timothy 3 4|1Ti.3:4]], 5 al.; of the Church, ὁ οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, [[1-timothy 3 15|1Ti.3:15]], [[hebrews 3 2|Heb.3:2]], [[1-peter 4 17|1Pe.4:17]]; of descendants, οἶ Ἰσραήλ (Δαυείδ, Ἰακώβ; Bl, §47, 9), [[matthew 10 6|Mat.10:6]], [[luke 1 27|Luk.1:27, 33]] al. (cf. [[exodus 6 14|Exo.6:14]], [[1-samuel 2 30|1Ki.2:30]], al.). SYN.: see: οἰκία. (AS)

οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;] 1. prop., a house, dwelling: [[acts 2 2|Act.2:2 19:16]]; with genitive poss., [[matthew 9 6|Mat.9:6]], 7 [[mark 2 11|Mrk.2:11]], [[luke 1 23|Luk.1:23]], al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, [[john 2 16|Jhn.2:16;]] προσευχῆς, [[matthew 21 13|Mat.21:13]], al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, [[matthew 12 4|Mat.12:4]], al.; the temple, [[matthew 21 13|Mat.21:13]], al.; metaphorically of a city: [[matthew 23 38|Mat.23:38]], [[luke 13 35|Luk.13:35]]; of the body, [[matthew 12 44|Mat.12:44]], [[luke 11 24|Luk.11:24]]; of Christians, [[1-peter 2 5|1Pe.2:5;]] ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, [[mark 2 1|Mrk.2:1]], [[1-corinthians 11 34|1Co.11:34 14:35]]; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, [[acts 2 46|Act.2:46 5:42]]; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., [[luke 7 10|Luk.7:10 15:6]]; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, [[acts 8 3|Act.8:3 20:20]]; εἰς (κατ ̓) οἶκον, with genitive (Bl., §46, 9), [[mark 8 3|Mrk.8:3]], [[luke 14 1|Luk.14:1]], [[romans 16 5|Rom.16:5]], al. 2. By meton., a house, household, family: [[luke 10 5|Luk.10:5]], [[acts 7 10|Act.7:10]], [[1-corinthians 1 16|1Co.1:16]], [[1-timothy 3 4|1Ti.3:4]], 5 al.; of the Church, ὁ οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, [[1-timothy 3 15|1Ti.3:15]], [[hebrews 3 2|Heb.3:2]], [[1-peter 4 17|1Pe.4:17]]; of descendants, οἶ Ἰσραήλ (Δαυείδ, Ἰακώβ; Bl, §47, 9), [[matthew 10 6|Mat.10:6]], [[luke 1 27|Luk.1:27, 33]] al. (cf. [[exodus 6 14|Exo.6:14]], [[1-samuel 2 30|1Ki.2:30]], al.). SYN.: see: οἰκία. (AS)

οἰκουμένη, -ης, ἡ (fern. Pres. pass. ptcp. of οἰκέω; sc. γῆ) [in LXX chiefly for תֵּבֵל, אֶרֶץ ;] the inhabited earth; (a) in cl., the countries occupied by Greeks, as disting. from barbarian lands (Hdt., Dem., al.); (b) in later writers, the Roman world: [[luke 2 1|Luk.2:1]], [[acts 11 28|Act.11:28 24:5]]; by meton., of its inhabitants : [[acts 17 6|Act.17:6 19:27]]; (with) in LXX ([[psalms 23 1|Psa.23:1 71:8]], al.) and NT, also of the whole inhabited world: [[matthew 24 14|Mat.24:14]], [[luke 4 5|Luk.4:5 21:26]], [[romans 10 18|Rom.10:18]], [[hebrews 1 6|Heb.1:6]], [[revelation 3 10|Rev.3:10 16:14]]; by meton. (ut supr.), [[acts 17 31|Act.17:31]], [[revelation 12 9|Rev.12:9]]; (d) of the Messianic age, ἡ οἰ. ἡ μέλλουσα = ὁ αἰὼ ὁ μέλλων: [[hebrews 2 5|Heb.2:5.]]† (AS)

οἰκ-ουρός, -ον (οἶκος + οὖρος, a keeper) 1. watching or keeping the house; as subst., ἡ οἰ., a housekeeper (Soph., Eur.; see LS, see word). 2. keeping at home: [[titus 2 5|Tit.2:5]], Rec. (see Field, Notes, 220 ff.; CGT, in l, and cf. οίκουργός).† (AS)
οἰκτείρω (οἶκτος, pity), [in LXX for רָחַם pi., חָנַן, etc. ;] to pity, have compassion on. with accusative of person(s), [[romans 9 15|Rom.9:15]] (LXX).† SYN.: ἐλεέω, q.v (AS)

ὀλιγό-πιστος, -ον of little faith or trust: [[matthew 6 30|Mat.6:30 8:26 14:31 16:8]], [[luke 12 28|Luk.12:28]].† (AS)

ὀλιγόφυχος, -ον [in LXX: [[isaiah 35 4|Isa.35:4]] (מָהַר ni.), etc. ;] faint-hearted: [[1-thessalonians 5 14|1Th.5:14.]]† (AS)

ὀλοκληρία, -ας, ἡ (ὁλόκληρος), [in LXX: [[isaiah 1 6|Isa.1:6]] (מְתֹם)* ;] completeness, soundness: [[acts 3 16|Act.3:16.]]† (AS)

ὁλό-κληρος, -ον (ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: [[leviticus 23 15|Lev.23:15]], [[ezekiel 15 5|Eze.15:5]] (תָּמִים), [[deuteronomy 27 6|Deu.27:6]], [[joshua 8 31|Jos.8:31]] (9:2) (שָׁלֵם), [[zechariah 11 16|Zec.11:16]] (נָצַב ni.), Wis.15:3, 1Ma.4:47, 4Ma.15:17 * ;] complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), [[1-thessalonians 5 23|1Th.5:23;]] ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, [[james 1 4|Jas.1:4.]]† SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii) (AS)
ὀλολύζω (onomatop.), [in LXX chiefly for יָלַל hi. ;] (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving), to cry aloud: [[james 5 1|Jas.5:1.]]† (AS)

ὅλος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for כֹּל ;] of persons and things, whole, entire, complete; 1. of indefinite ideas, with subst. anarth.: [[luke 5 5|Luk.5:5]], [[acts 11 26|Act.11:26 28:30]], [[titus 1 11|Tit.1:11]]; ὅλον ἄνθρωπον (an entire man; see Field, Notes, 93), [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23;]] ὅλη Ἰερουσαλήμ (= πᾶσα Ἰ, [[matthew 2 3|Mat.2:3;]] see Bl., §47, 9), [[acts 21 31|Act.21:31.]] 2. ὁλοτελής, -ές (ὅλος, τίλος), complete, perfect.. [[1-thessalonians 5 23|1Th.5:23.]]† SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. Ὀλυμπᾶς (perh. contr. fr. Ὀλνμπιόδωρος, Bl., § 29), -ᾶ, Olympas: [[romans 16 15|Rom.16:15.]]† (AS)
ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: [[song-of-solomon 2 13|Sng.2:13]] (פַּג)* ;] an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring : [[revelation 6 13|Rev.6:13.]]† (AS)

ὄμβρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 32 2|Deu.32:2]] (שָׂעִיר), Wis.16:16, al. ;] a storm of rain, a shower: [[luke 12 54|Luk.12:54.]]† (AS)

ὁμιλέω, -ῶ (ὅμιλος), [in LXX: [[proverbs 5 19|Pro.5:19]] (רָוָה pi.), al. ;] to be in company with, consort with; hence, to converse with: [[acts 20 11|Act.20:11;]] with dative, [[acts 24 26|Act.24:26;]] before πρός, [[luke 24 14|Luk.24:14-15.]]† (AS)
όμιλία, -ας, ή (όμιλος), [in LXX: [[exodus 21 10|Exo.21:10]] (עוֹנָה), al. ;] company, association: [[1-corinthians 15 33|1Co.15:33.]]† (AS)
ὅμιλος, -ου, ὁ [in Aq. : [[1-samuel 19 20|1Ki.19:20]] * ;] a crowd, throng: [[revelation 18 17|Rev.18:17]], Rec.† (AS)
ὄμμα, -τος, τό in cl. chiefly poët.; [in LXX for עַיִן (עַיִן ([[proverbs 5 1|Pro.5:1-23]], Wis.2:1-24, 4Ma.3:1-21)* ;] an eye: p1., [[matthew 20 34|Mat.20:34]] [[mark 8 23|Mrk.8:23]].† (AS)

ὁμοιάζω (ὅμοιος), to be like: [[matthew 23 27|Mat.23:27]] (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) [[matthew 26 73|Mat.26:73]] (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.) † (AS)
ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές (ὅμοιος, πάσχω), [in LXX: Wis.7:3, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] of like feelings or affections: with dative, [[acts 14 15|Act.14:15]], [[james 5 17|Jas.5:17]].† (AS)

ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ (όμολογέω), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 12 6|Deu.12:6, 17]]. ὁμοῦ adv. (ὁμός), together; (a) prop., of place: [[john 21 2|Jhn.21:2]], [[acts 2 1|Act.2:1]]; (b) without idea of place: [[john 4 36|Jhn.4:36 20:4]].† (AS)
